cover: Questions to ask before you trust an AI agent

slides.title: What tools can it use?
slides.body: And with whose permissions? Each tool should have only the access a person in that role would need.

slides.title: What may it do without asking?
slides.body: Get it in writing: what it does on its own, what needs a person's OK and what it must never try.

slides.title: What does it do when it isn't sure?
slides.body: Look for step limits, timeouts and a set point where it gives up, so it stops or hands off when it's stuck.

slides.title: Who checks its work?
slides.body: Agents tend to rate their own work too highly. The check should be separate from the agent.

slides.title: Can you see every action it took?
slides.body: You want a log of every action, what it was given and why it acted.

slides.title: Has it been tested on awkward cases?
slides.body: Ask for scored test runs on realistic cases, like a missing attachment, before it goes near a real inbox.
